title: Output-polynomial hypergraph transversal enumeration
formal: Do a deterministic Turing algorithm \(A\) and absolute constants \(C,c>0\) exist such that, for every explicitly given finite hypergraph \(H\), \(A\) outputs every inclusion-minimal transversal exactly once and terminates within \(C(L(H)+L_{\mathrm{out}}(H)+1)^c\) bit steps?
why: This central enumeration question governs the complexity of converting a hypergraph into the family of all its minimal hitting sets and underlies many enumeration reductions.
status_note: Explicitly open in the August 2026 primary preprint. Its negative result applies to MMCS, not to all algorithms. The original formulation and later abstract were checked on 13 September 2026; no exhaustive literature claim is made.
review_note: Completed individual source and formulation review on 13 September 2026; see statement_review and research/card-completion-20260913/reviews.jsonl.

category_assignment.reason: The target is output-polynomial enumeration of minimal hypergraph transversals, so it returns to the enumeration category.

importance.reason: A central longstanding enumeration problem and a reference point for the complexity of many other complete-output tasks.

definitions: \(H=([n],E), n\ge 0\), is supplied as the explicit vertex list and a finite list of edges \(e\subseteq [n]\), each edge an increasing list of binary vertex identifiers. Repeated edges have no effect. \(\mathrm{L}(H)\) is the bit length of this input including delimiters. A transversal is a set \(T\subseteq [n]\) intersecting every \(e\in E\); it is inclusion-minimal when no proper subset has this property. Output each such T as an increasing list of its binary vertex identifiers with a delimiter, in arbitrary order; no duplicate, nonminimal or incomplete output is allowed. \(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{out}}(H)\) is the sum of the bit lengths of these records, counting one delimiter even for \(T=\varnothing\). If E is empty, the unique minimal transversal is \(\varnothing\). If E contains \(\varnothing\), there is no transversal and \(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{out}}=0\). Time includes all computation, output and termination detection. The polynomial and algorithm are independent of n, E, edge size and output size; there is no separate delay or workspace bound, advice, oracle or randomization. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof of a single algorithm meeting the total output-polynomial bound, including completeness, uniqueness and termination on every finite hypergraph, or a Lean proof that none exists. The target imposes no polynomial-delay or polynomial-space bound. A lower bound for one enumeration algorithm does not establish nonexistence of all algorithms.

sentences: A transversal meets every edge of a hypergraph and is minimal if removing any selected vertex destroys that property.
The required algorithm lists all such sets exactly once and detects when enumeration is finished.
Its total time must be polynomial in the combined input and complete output length.
The output may be exponentially large, and no separate bound on delay is requested.
A 2026 lower bound excludes a particular practical algorithm while leaving the existence of a general output-polynomial algorithm open.

context_blocks.text: Minimal transversals are the irredundant ways to hit every edge of a hypergraph. Their number may be exponential in the input size, so the target charges time against the complete output as well as the input.
The August 2026 MMCS lower bound concerns one particular enumeration algorithm. The same paper explicitly retains the existence of some output-polynomial algorithm as open.
